children: Paramount Skydance Corp. (PSKY, Financials), the media company pursuing a $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, may be preparing for a dramatic change in its relationship with California.
TMZ reported that officials in Los Angeles and the California Attorney General's office had been told Paramount planned to announce it was leaving the state. But the expected announcement never came.
It remains unclear whether the plan changed or was simply delayed, making the report another source of uncertainty around Paramount's much larger battle over Warner Bros. Discovery.

California and 11 other states sued in July to block the acquisition, arguing the combination could reduce competition and increase prices in film and television. The financial clock is already running.
Paramount has said delays beyond Sept. 30 trigger a $7 million daily payment to Warner Bros. shareholders. It has also sought a $1.88 billion bond from the states challenging the transaction.
There may still be room for a resolution. Paramount, California Attorney General Rob Bonta and the Writers Guild of America are scheduled to hold settlement discussions Oct. 14-15.

For investors, that meeting now carries even more weight. The question is whether Paramount can resolve the California fight before the cost and uncertainty surrounding its biggest deal climb further.

title: Paramount's Warner Bros. Fight Just Took an Unexpected Turn
